note: M31: spies. Every great power keeps a network in each other realm, 0 to 100 deep. Each month a network grows by growth times its master's skill / 50, times the target's openness, times what is spent (budgetFactor: the crown's budget against budgetFull, at least minFactor; an AI power spends by its own spend), less the target's own counter-espionage (homeGuard, cutting growth by its value / guardCut), and loses decay (a share) of its depth, so each settles where growth and fading meet. Starting depths are from the lore: Nilfgaard's networks grow fastest everywhere, Redania's (Dijkstra) are the deepest in the North, Kaedwen's crude, Aedirn's modest. Petty and middle crowns keep only a guard at home. unlocks name what each depth shows or allows (operations come with Part B). The crown's spymaster is chosen from candidates (skill and a trait); the office costs wage crowns a month (without one the crown's networks grow at owners.temeria.skill), and a deep foreign network at home may buy or kill the spymaster (turnAt, turnChance, killAt, killChance a month, less for a loyal or cautious master).

unlocks.text: Its armies, treasury and treaties; its armies seen on the map
Its ruler's plans, and its own spies in Temeria
Bribe a lord, a governor or a petty king
Stir the Scoia'tael or a peasant revolt
Sabotage works or a siege camp's stores
Assassinate a commander, a lord or a spymaster

operations.note: M31 B: what a network deep enough can do (at: the depth needed). Each costs coin and puts the realm's networks on cooldown (days). It may be exposed: risk x the target's watch / 40 (Temeria adds a quarter of the spymaster's skill to it) x the spymaster's trait (cautious less, ruthless more), less as depth passes the need (to half at 25 points over), at most maxRisk. Exposed, it fails: the network loses depthLoss, the ruler's trust in the crown falls by trust (half again with a ruthless spymaster) and their relation by relation, and one time in agentLostChance the agent is taken (a further agentLostDepth).

counter.note: M31 C: foreign networks in Temeria. Each month each foreign network may lose an agent to the crown's watch: catchBase x its depth / 50 x the crown's watch / 40 (homeGuard, a quarter of the spymaster's skill, and the counterSpy of laws: curfews, the king's riders, the inquisition), at most catchMax, one caught agent before the crown at a time and none within gapDays of the last. A caught agent is a decision: hang (Fear, their network hurt, their ruler angry), turn (our network in their realm deepens, or the agent was playing us), trade back (trust and goodwill, a smaller dent), or follow (their network rolled up a little, its depth known for a year, and a traitor spymaster in their pay unmasked). Foreign networks also work against Temeria (foreignOps, a month's chance x the owner's spend; triple at war with us, double for the Empire under pressure), at the depth each needs; the crown's watch may catch them at it (the operation's risk x watch / 40). Their work leaves a clue; a spymaster may later name who did it (nameChance a month x skill / 50).
